note: Re-judged 2026-11-19. RFC 4301 Section 4.4.1: "If the SPD is not decorrelated, caching is not allowed and an ordered search of SPD MUST be performed to verify that inbound traffic arriving on an SA is consistent with the access control policy expressed in the SPD." Since the state-selector binding the SA selector refuses an out-of-SA packet before the SPD is searched, so the tests were reworked. Positive TestRFC4301OrderedInboundSearchAdmitsOnTheFirstRankedEntry now narrows only the installed inbound PROTECT entry to 10.1.0.0/24 while the SA keeps 10.1.0.0/16, reads back the Child entry at PriorityChildSA allow over the catch-all, and proves three outcomes: a packet inside the PROTECT entry is delivered with XfrmInPolBlock unchanged; a packet inside the SA but outside the first-ranked PROTECT entry (10.1.1.5) is not delivered and moves XfrmInPolBlock by exactly one (the catch-all DISCARD decided after decryption); a packet outside the SA moves only XfrmInStateMismatch. That isolates the ordered SPD search on traffic the SA admitted, which is stronger than before. Negative TestRFC4301OrderedInboundSearchRefusesOnTheFirstRankedDiscard is unchanged (an operator inbound DISCARD ranked 1000 over the Child entry drops an in-selector packet on the SA, XfrmInPolBlock +1). The boundary SPD units are unchanged. Finding: TestRFC4301ParallelSAsAreHeldToTheOneSharedPolicy keeps an RFC4301-4.4.1-10 negative tag, but its body now asserts the refusal at the SA selector before any SPD lookup (XfrmInStateMismatch +1, XfrmInNoPols and XfrmInPolBlock unchanged); its claim says so honestly, yet it no longer evidences the SPD search this row requires. The verdict rests on the ordered pair; that tag should move to the SAD-selector rows (RFC4301-5.2-2, 5.2-11) or be removed, under ze-test-judge.
